text:
sara_ng: kicking off canary for latency-sentinel batch quota scrub. target: p95 <= 120ms for route: chat:premium (tier A). rolling kernel switch to opt-kernel-v2 + dynamic-token-budgeter enabled for 5% of traffic.

vikram_p: saw p95 drift ~30ms on initial runs, looks correlated with KV miss rate spike after kernel switch. capturing traces now.

linh_hoa: uploaded flamegraphs and a short profile -> https://artifacts.internal/redwood/perf/7823456789/flame.svg  please check the hot path around kv::lookup + batcher::enqueue.

linh_hoa: current canary budget config (posted for visibility):
```yaml
route: chat:premium
p95_target_ms: 120
token_budget:
  base: 48
  dynamic: true
  max: 256
batch_formation:
  max_wait_ms: 8
  min_batch_tokens: 32
queue_policy:
  prefer_fill_on_kv_miss: false
```

perf-bot: Alert at 7823456790 -> p95 breach for chat:premium: 155ms (window: 1m). hosts affected: gpu-23,gpu-19.

hugo: hypothesis: opt-kernel-v2 has worse latency for short, sparse microbatches (more kernel init overhead). it wins once batches are larger. the dynamic token budget increases batch variance which exposes that overhead.

vikram_p: proposal: change queue_policy to `prefer_fill_on_kv_miss: true` so batcher waits up to +4ms to try to assemble larger microbatches when KV miss rate climbs. tradeoff: slight added tail wait vs better kernel throughput.

sara_ng: applied the queue tweak to canary at 7823456800 and bumped observability to surface batch_size histogram and kv_hit_rate.

linh_hoa: after tweak p95 dropped to ~118ms on the canary window (10m), kv_hit_rate stabilized ~+6pp, but token utilization went down ~12% (cost up ~3%).

vikram_p: that's promising. we should quantify p95 vs cost curve before widening. also the kernel selection score needs to consider `batch_shape_score` from the profiler so we don't pick opt-kernel-v2 for tiny batches.

perf-bot: Captured longer flamegraph at 7823456815 -> https://artifacts.internal/redwood/perf/7823456815/flame.svg (note increased CPU sys time during prefetch path).

hugo: also saw KV cache churn when dynamic_token_budget grew beyond ~128 for a session: eviction spikes and degraded hit rate. suggestion: enforce `session_token_cap` and ramp rate. e.g., cap=192 and ramp +10 tokens per successful request up to cap.

sara_ng: agreed. will add `session_token_cap: 192` and `ramp_step: 10` to config and do a gradual roll (5% -> 20%). tagging @eng-sre for oncall watch.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout to 5% completed at 7823456810 :rocket: (config: prefer_fill_on_kv_miss=true, session_token_cap not yet applied).

linh_hoa: quick dev note — found a small regression: kernel-prefetch path disables prefetch for microbatches <64 tokens which increases CPU overhead on the host. opened PR #1248 to re-enable a lightweight prefetch for short batches.

vikram_p: thanks. next actions (tracking):
- apply session_token_cap + ramping to canary (sara)
- add batch_shape scoring into kernel selector (hugo)
- run extended canary 2h, then promote to 20% if stable (sara)
- measure p95/p99 and cost delta, collect KV eviction metrics (linh)

sara_ng: good plan. extending canary to 2h now. will post a summary if we hit stability targets. :white_check_mark:
